Subject: Question on billing when we mix short prompts + long retrievals

Hi Grace,

Quick question from our implementation team as we build a chat assistant: users will frequently alternate between very short prompts (1–2 tokens of user text — e.g., "yes/no" confirmations or quick help) and long retrieval responses where we concatenate 8–15k tokens of context before generation.

The specific asks: 
- Will those short interleaved prompts be billed separately as their own "session" minimums or aggregated into the long context window?
- How does rounding work if one short prompt is followed immediately by a long retrieval in the same user session?
- If we stitch multiple retrievals together (some overlapping), do we pay for the raw concatenated context length or is there dedup/kv-cache behavior on metering?

We want to model costs for a proof-of-concept and also understand whether a custom pricing floor or rounding exemption is something to discuss for our pilot.

Thanks — can you point us to a short example we can show the engineering and finance teams?

—Hannah

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the clear examples — great questions. Short answer up front: we bill per-request tokens (prompt + completion) but we also have conversation-window aggregation rules and a per-call minimum that can affect small rapid prompts. I'll summarize with concrete examples below and then loop in Finance/PD to confirm edge cases and a recommended pilot credit or rounding concession.

Examples:
1) Short prompt alone (user says "OK"): billed as one request; if it falls below the per-request minimum (e.g., 32 token floor) it's rounded up to the floor.
2) Short prompt immediately followed by a long retrieval in the same session: if the two requests are within the same conversation window (we define this by a short idle timeout and conversation-id), only the raw tokens for each request are billed — they do not auto-merge for billing. However, our platform applies prefix caching for repeated context which can reduce compute tokens. Billing-wise you still see prompt tokens for the concatenated context used in that generation call.
3) Stitched retrievals with overlap: we meter on the final concatenated prompt that the model receives. We do not automatically dedupe overlapping content at billing time; deduplication is an optimization that can be enabled in the client to avoid sending repeated bytes.

I'll confirm the policy on "aggregation windows" and whether we can offer an experimental smoothing rule for your pilot (e.g., aggregate small consecutive requests within X seconds into a single billing unit) — Marissa / Ben, can you weigh in on what pilot concession we'd be comfortable with?

I'll attach a tiny spreadsheet with worked examples for your team and a sample trace from a real pilot.

- Hannah: if you'd like, we'll run a 1-week usage trace against your sample workload and show a line-by-line invoice simulation.

Grace —

Copied Tessa for approval on any pilot concession. Quick internal summary / recommendation:

Policy clarifications (finance):
- Metering base: we bill the exact token count sent to the model for each generation call (prompt + completion), subject to the per-call minimum of 32 tokens. There is no automatic dedupe across separate calls for billing.
- Aggregation rule: we currently support a 90s conversation-window that can optionally be extended to 180s for pilots. Within that window we do NOT merge two network calls into one billed call — billing is per RPC. The only exception is when the SDK is used with our "bundler" mode that explicitly concatenates short calls client-side and sends a single request; in that case you will be billed for that single concatenated prompt.

Pilot concession idea (commercial):
- Offer: For the 8-week pilot, we can apply a smoothing credit where we waive the 32-token floor for up to 10k small interleaved requests per month (i.e., bill exact tokens instead of rounding up for those events). This is limited to usage traced to the pilot conversation-ids and requires us to ingest a short trace to validate.
- Rationale: keeps instrumented early usage representative while protecting Redwood from heavy abuse.

Attachments included: pricing_examples.xlsx (worked examples for mixed flows), usage_trace_sample.jsonl (obfuscated trace format we can replay).

Ben — confirm that concession is acceptable from a finance standpoint and whether we need a PO/AMENDMENT.

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the patience. We dug into this and attached a short spreadsheet with line-item examples; key points below (TL;DR at top):

TL;DR:
- Billing is per-request (prompt+completion). Short interleaved prompts are billed as separate calls and will hit the 32-token floor unless you use our SDK bundler or we enable the pilot smoothing credit.
- Stitched retrievals are billed on the final concatenated prompt size we receive; there is no automatic dedupe for billing.
- For your pilot, we can enable a temporary smoothing exemption (waive the 32-token floor for up to 10k small requests/month) and run a 1-week invoice simulation from your trace.

Concrete example pulled from pricing_examples.xlsx:
- Case A: User sends "Yes" (3 tokens) -> model completion (20 tokens) in isolation = meter charges 32-token floor.
- Case B: User sends "Yes" (3 tokens), <2s later the system sends a retrieval+prompt (12,000 tokens) -> billed as two requests: 32-token floor for request A, and 12,000 + completion tokens for request B. If you bundle A + B client-side and send as a single RPC the billing is for the combined prompt.

Next steps if you want to proceed:
1) Share an anonymized 48–72 hour trace (we accepted the sample earlier).
2) We'll run a line-by-line invoice simulation and share a short report with cost breakdown and percent of events that would have hit the floor vs exact token billing.
3) If the pilot looks like the expected profile, Marissa will provision the smoothing credit and Ben will confirm amendment/PO language.
